title: Brain: Add access heat tracking for smarter consolidation
description:
## Problem
All 212 LTM entries are equal citizens. `family.anniversary` (recalled constantly) has the same weight as `solar.inverter_firmware_version` (touched once, months ago). Consolidation has no signal for which entries are actually useful, so it cannot make intelligent pruning decisions.

## Proposal
Track access frequency and recency for every Brain entry. Use these signals during consolidation to promote frequently-used working memory and demote untouched LTM entries.

### Fields to Add
- `access_count: int` — incremented on every `get` or `recall` hit
- `last_accessed: timestamp` — updated on every `get` or `recall` hit
- `created_at: timestamp` — already exists, confirm it is indexed

### Heat Score
Calculate a composite heat score during consolidation:

```
heat = (access_count * 0.4) + (recency_bonus * 0.4) + (salience * 0.2)
```

Where `recency_bonus` decays over time (e.g., 1.0 if accessed today, 0.5 if within 7 days, 0.1 if >30 days).

### Consolidation Behavior Changes
- **Promotion (working → LTM):** Prioritize entries with high access count. If a working entry was recalled 5+ times this session, promote it.
- **Demotion (LTM → working or evict):** Entries in LTM with `access_count == 0` and `age > 30 days` should be flagged for demotion or eviction.
- **Status reporting:** `Brain.status` should show top-10 hottest keys and top-10 coldest (candidates for pruning).

### Implementation Notes
- Access tracking should be lightweight — increment a counter, update a timestamp. No heavy computation at access time.
- Heat score is computed during consolidation, not at access time.
- `recall` results should optionally include heat metadata so the agent can see which facts are well-established vs. speculative.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every `get` and `recall` hit increments `access_count` and updates `last_accessed`
- [ ] Consolidation uses heat score for promotion/demotion decisions
- [ ] `status` reports hottest and coldest entries
- [ ] Existing entries backfilled with default access_count=0

Problem
=======
Gateway.update_config is a stub (internal/api/status_ops.go:80, verified 2026-09-17). Config changes to the AI/provider section require a full gateway restart (Jeff-gated), which kills all active sessions. Implementation
==============
1. In internal/api/status_ops.go, replace the stub with: parse JSON body -> validate against config schema (mirror the validation that runs at startup in the config loader) -> apply in-memory swap under the existing config mutex -> persist to config.json atomically (write temp + rename) -> return the applied config.
2. Scope: apply live only to hot-swappable sections — ai.providers (name, api_key env ref, model, models list, timeout_seconds, fallback, max_concurrent once conduit-38cz lands), channels enabled/disabled flags, tools policy. If any section is not hot-swappable (e.g. server port, ssh), reject with a 400 listing the offending keys rather than silently ignoring.

4. Reuse the reload pattern from reload_skills (internal/api/skills*.go) for lifecycle/locking. Channel enable/disable via update_config must reuse the same code path as the existing enable_channel/disable_channel actions so state stays consistent.
5. Emit a gateway log line + metric on every successful apply (section list, who/what session).

Tests
=====
- Table-driven tests in internal/api: valid provider patch applies and readback matches; invalid model name rejected with 422 and config unchanged; port change rejected; concurrent apply during an in-flight LLM call does not race (race detector on).
- A test that config.json on disk matches in-memory applied state after apply, including ${ENV_VAR} refs preserved (do not expand secrets into the file).

Acceptance
==========
From a live gateway: change z-ai timeout_seconds via the Gateway tool, verify next LLM call uses it, no restart, active sessions intact.

title: Brain: Auto-extract and cache facts from file reads
description:
## Problem
Every fact stored in Brain requires an explicit `Brain.store()` call. When reading a file like `reference/energy.md`, the agent must manually identify useful facts and make separate tool calls for each one. This is tedious and error-prone — facts get missed when the agent forgets to cache them, meaning subsequent sessions re-read the same files.

## Proposal
After a file read, automatically extract and cache the top N key facts into Brain working memory. The agent can then promote the useful ones during consolidation instead of relying on manual discipline.

### Approach: Template-Based Extraction Hints
Rather than doing heavy NLP on every file read, allow files to declare extraction hints in a structured format:

```markdown
<!-- brain-extract
solar.panel_count: "30"
solar.inverter_model: "Acme 10kW"
solar.battery_capacity: "20 kWh (2x 14.6)"
/brain-extract -->
```

When Brain (or the agent harness) reads a file containing these hints, it automatically stores the declared facts into working memory.

### Alternative: Agent-Prompted Bulk Store
Add a `Brain.store_bulk` action that accepts multiple key-value pairs in one call:

```
Brain.store_bulk(entries=[
  {key: "solar.panel_count", value: "30"},
  {key: "solar.inverter_model", value: "Acme 10kW"},
  {key: "solar.battery_capacity", value: "20 kWh"}
], tier="working")
```

This reduces the friction from N tool calls to 1.

### Recommended Implementation
Do both:
1. `store_bulk` — low effort, high impact on agent workflow
2. Template hints in reference files — zero-effort caching for stable reference docs

### Implementation Notes
- `store_bulk` should be atomic — all entries succeed or all fail
- Template hints should be parseable with a simple regex, no complex parser needed
- Hints are optional — files without them work exactly as before
- Consider a `brain-extract-ignore` directive for sections to skip
- Auto-extracted entries should have a source tag (e.g., `source: "file:reference/energy.md"`) so they can be traced and refreshed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `store_bulk` action accepts array of key-value pairs
- [ ] Files with `<!-- brain-extract ... -->` blocks auto-cache on read
- [ ] Auto-cached entries tagged with source file
- [ ] Both features are opt-in — no behavior change for existing files/calls

title: prompt_builder: drop duplicated tool descriptions from Tooling section
description:
Why: The Tooling section of the system prompt restates tool descriptions that are ALREADY sent verbatim in the tools array with every LLM call — pure duplication paid on every invocation. At ~2,600 invocations/day (Sep 26 journal) that is ~8M+ tokens/day of duplicated description text before caching. Direct cost, zero information gain.

- debug_prompt on live gateway: Tooling section = 13,259 chars of 50,506 total (~3.3K tokens/invocation)
- internal/agent/prompt_builder.go buildToolingSection() emits '- Name: Description' lines from the same schema description strings carried in the tools array
- Skill-derived tools are already compressed to a single line in main source (good) — but live gateway still shows full fat, so running binary likely predates it; verify at next deploy
- Remaining fat: ~23 built-in tools with full descriptions (Bash ~470 chars, Brain ~1.5K, Message ~1.1K, Cron ~900, ...)

Proposal:
- Tooling section lists tool NAMES only, or name + ≤6-word category hint
- Keep the policy lines (case-sensitivity note, TOOLS.md guidance note, SessionsSpawn delegation note)
- Full descriptions remain solely in the tools array where the API consumes them

Acceptance criteria:
- debug_prompt Tooling section < 2,000 chars
- prompt_builder_test.go expectations updated
- No regression: agent tool-call accuracy unchanged in smoke test

title: AI prompt builder duplicates current user message (store-then-append)
description: Root cause of doubled user messages in LLM prompts. Gateway stores incoming user message to session DB (gateway.go:1028) BEFORE calling AI, then passes msg.Text as userMessage to GenerateResponse*/GenerateResponseStreaming (router.go:597,767,1033). buildChatMessagesWithSystemPrompt (internal/ai/messages.go) loads recent history — which already contains the just-stored message — then appends userMessage again at the end. Result: every user message appears TWICE in the prompt. Telegram is NOT the cause: adapter dedups by update_id, 7 days of logs show zero 'Duplicate update' skips, and the current message exists exactly once in gateway.db (row 6a82ac8d). Repro: internal/ai/messages_dup_repro_test.go (fails: expected 1 copy, got 2). Fix options: (a) skip trailing history user message when content == userMessage in buildChatMessages*, or (b) exclude messages stored after the last assistant response from history. Option (a) is surgical; keep store-before-call semantics (persistence on AI failure). Also consider: goal-refocus reminder (execution.go:512) repeats identical 'Reminder: Your original goal was...' at each refocus depth — cosmetic amplifier, same text every time.
close_reason: done
